{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_4","type":"command_execution","command":"/bin/bash -lc \"sed -n '1,260p' /app/convert_data.py\"","aggregated_output":"\"\"\"\nConvert neural data from Zhong et al. 2025 \"Unsupervised pretraining in biological neural networks\"\ninto the standardized decoder format.\n\nProcessing follows the reference paper and code:\n- Neural data: deconvolved calcium traces from Suite2p, position-interpolated to 60 bins per corridor\n- Only texture area bins (0-39) are used (40 bins = 4m corridor at 1 dm resolution)\n- Only visual cortex neurons are included (iarea != -1 and iarea != 7)\n- Only running frames are used for interpolation (VR moving, ft_move > 0)\n- Brain regions: V1 (iarea=8), mHV (iarea in 0,1,2,9), lHV (iarea in 5,6), aHV (iarea in 3,4)\n\"\"\"\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport os\nimport pickle\nimport sys\nfrom datetime import datetime\nimport gc\n\nROOT = 'data'\nN_POS_BINS = 60       # Total position bins per corridor (paper convention)\nN_TEXTURE_BINS = 40   # Texture area bins (0-39, = 4m corridor)\nVR_SPEED = 6.0        # dm/s (60 cm/s)\nBIN_SIZE_SEC = 1.0 / VR_SPEED  # seconds per position bin = 1/6 s ≈ 0.1667s\nBIN_SIZE_MS = BIN_SIZE_SEC * 1000  # ≈ 166.67 ms\n\n\ndef position_interpolate_spk(raw_spk, accum_pos, corridor_len, n_trials, n_bins=60):\n    \"\"\"Position-interpolate spike data to evenly spaced position bins.\n\n    Matches utils.spk_pos_interp and utils.get_interpPos_spk from the paper code.\n    Uses numpy.interp for speed (equivalent to scipy interp1d with extrapolation).\n\n    Args:\n        raw_spk: (n_neurons, n_frames) - neural data for running frames only\n        accum_pos: (n_frames,) - cumulative position for running frames\n        corridor_len: corridor length in dm\n        n_trials: number of trials\n        n_bins: bins per corridor\n\n    Returns:\n        interp_spk: (n_neurons, n_trials, n_bins)\n    \"\"\"\n    lin_pos = np.arange(0, n_trials, 1.0 / n_bins)\n    norm_pos = accum_pos / corridor_len\n    n_neurons = raw_spk.shape[0]\n    n_target = len(lin_pos)\n    interp_spk = np.zeros((n_neurons, n_target), dtype=np.float32)\n\n    # Use numpy.interp which is much faster than scipy for 1D interpolation\n    for s in range(n_neurons):\n        interp_spk[s, :] = np.interp(lin_pos, norm_pos, raw_spk[s, :])\n\n    return interp_spk.reshape(n_neurons, n_trials, n_bins)\n\n\ndef get_brain_region_idx(iarea):\n    \"\"\"Map iarea values to brain region indices.\n\n    Brain regions (from paper's neu_area_ID):\n        V1: iarea == 8\n        mHV: iarea in {0, 1, 2, 9}\n        lHV: iarea in {5, 6}\n        aHV: iarea in {3, 4}\n\n    Returns:\n        region_idx: array of region indices (0=V1, 1=mHV, 2=lHV, 3=aHV)\n        valid_mask: boolean mask for neurons in visual cortex\n    \"\"\"\n    valid_mask = (iarea != -1) & (iarea != 7)\n    region_idx = np.full(len(iarea), -1, dtype=int)\n    region_idx[iarea == 8] = 0  # V1\n    region_idx[(iarea == 0) | (iarea == 1) | (iarea == 2) | (iarea == 9)] = 1  # mHV\n    region_idx[(iarea == 5) | (iarea == 6)] = 2  # lHV\n    region_idx[(iarea == 3) | (iarea == 4)] = 3  # aHV\n    return region_idx, valid_mask\n\n\ndef lick_to_position_bins(lick_pos, lick_trind, n_trials, n_bins=40):\n    \"\"\"Convert lick events to binary per-position-bin per-trial.\n\n    Args:\n        lick_pos: position of each lick event (in dm)\n        lick_trind: trial index of each lick event\n        n_trials: number of trials\n        n_bins: number of position bins (texture area)\n\n    Returns:\n        lick_binary: (n_trials, n_bins) binary array\n    \"\"\"\n    lick_binary = np.zeros((n_trials, n_bins), dtype=int)\n    for i in range(len(lick_pos)):\n        tr = int(lick_trind[i])\n        pos = lick_pos[i]\n        bin_idx = int(pos)\n        if 0 <= bin_idx < n_bins and 0 <= tr < n_trials:\n            lick_binary[tr, bin_idx] = 1\n    return lick_binary\n\n\ndef compute_day_of_training(date_str):\n    \"\"\"Parse date string like '2022_08_17' to datetime.\"\"\"\n    return datetime.strptime(date_str, '%Y_%m_%d')\n\n\ndef collect_all_sessions(exp_info, root):\n    \"\"\"Collect all unique recording sessions with their metadata.\n\n    For recordings appearing in multiple experiment types, use the first one found.\n    Returns list of session dicts with all needed info.\n    \"\"\"\n    seen_recordings = set()\n    sessions = []\n\n    # Process experiment types in a specific order to prefer more complete annotations\n    # Prefer test sessions (more stimuli) over train sessions (fewer stimuli)\n    exp_order = sorted(exp_info.keys(), key=lambda x: (\n        0 if 'test' in x else 1,  # test first\n        0 if 'sup_' in x else 1,  # supervised first (has rewards)\n        0 if 'after' in x else 1,  # after learning first\n        x  # alphabetical tiebreak\n    ))\n\n    for exp_type in exp_order:\n        db_list = exp_info[exp_type]\n        # Load behavior data\n        beh_path = os.path.join(root, 'beh', f'Beh_{exp_type}.npy')\n        if not os.path.exists(beh_path):\n            print(f\"  Warning: behavior file not found for {exp_type}\")\n            continue\n        beh_data = np.load(beh_path, allow_pickle=True).item()\n\n        for ndb in db_list:\n            rec_key = (ndb['mname'], ndb['datexp'], ndb['blk'])\n            if rec_key in seen_recordings:\n                continue\n            seen_recordings.add(rec_key)\n\n            # Build behavior key\n            stimtype = ndb.get('stimtype', '')\n            if stimtype:\n                beh_key = f\"{ndb['mname']}_{ndb['datexp']}_{ndb['blk']}_{stimtype}\"\n            else:\n                beh_key = f\"{ndb['mname']}_{ndb['datexp']}_{ndb['blk']}\"\n\n            if beh_key not in beh_data:\n                print(f\"  Warning: behavior key {beh_key} not found in {exp_type}\")\n                continue\n\n            sessions.append({\n                'mname': ndb['mname'],\n                'datexp': ndb['datexp'],\n                'blk': ndb['blk'],\n                'exp_type': exp_type,\n                'beh_key': beh_key,\n                'beh': beh_data[beh_key],\n                'ndb': ndb,\n            })\n\n    return sessions\n\n\ndef process_session(session_info, root, all_stim_names, speed_quantile_edges):\n    \"\"\"Process a single recording session into decoder format.\n\n    Args:\n        session_info: dict with session metadata and behavior\n        root: data root directory\n        all_stim_names: list of all unique stimulus names (for consistent labeling)\n        speed_quantile_edges: pre-computed quartile edges for running speed\n\n    Returns:\n        dict with neural, input, output, brain_region_idx for this session\n    \"\"\"\n    ndb = session_info['ndb']\n    beh = session_info['beh']\n    mname = ndb['mname']\n    datexp = ndb['datexp']\n    blk = ndb['blk']\n\n    # Load neural data\n    spk_fn = f\"{mname}_{datexp}_{blk}_neural_data.npy\"\n    spk_data = np.load(os.path.join(root, 'spk', spk_fn), allow_pickle=True).item()\n    spk = np.concatenate([s for s in spk_data['spks']], axis=0)\n    del spk_data\n    n_neurons, n_frames = spk.shape\n\n    # Load retinotopy\n    ret_fn = f\"{mname}_{datexp}_trans.npz\"\n    ret_data = np.load(os.path.join(root, 'retinotopy', ret_fn), allow_pickle=True)\n    iarea = ret_data['iarea']\n\n    # Get valid neuron mask (visual cortex only)\n    region_idx, valid_mask = get_brain_region_idx(iarea)\n    valid_neurons = valid_mask\n\n    # Get behavior variables\n    n_trials = beh['ntrials']\n    corridor_len = beh['Corridor_Length']  # typically 60 dm\n\n    # Filter for running frames (VR moving)\n    ft_move = beh['ft_move'][:n_frames]\n    vr_moving = ft_move > 0\n    ft_pos_cum = beh['ft_PosCum'][:n_frames]\n\n    # 375→\\n   376→def get_dist_img(xpos, ypos, sel_idx=None, sig=30, sig_bg=30, xoff=800, yoff=800):\\n   377→    from scipy import ndimage\\n   378→    \\\"\\\"\\\"create an binary image for indicate 375→\\n   376→def get_dist_img(xpos, ypos, sel_idx=None, sig=30, sig_bg=30, xoff=800, yoff=800):\\n   377→    from scipy import ndimage\\n   378→    \\\"\\\"\\\"create an binary image for indicate 912→\\n   913→def spk_2_firstLick(spk, beh, ranges=[15, 15], bins=30):\\n   914→    \\\"\\\"\\\"ranges: frames included before and after first lick\\n   915→        spk: one dimensional activity\\n   916→    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n   917→    lickPos, lickFr, lickTr, ntrials  = beh['LickPos'], beh['LickFr'].astype(int), beh['LickTrind'].astype(int), beh['ntrials']\\n   918→    spk2Flick = 375→\\n   376→def get_dist_img(xpos, ypos, sel_idx=None, sig=30, sig_bg=30, xoff=800, yoff=800):\\n   377→    from scipy import ndimage\\n   378→    \\\"\\\"\\\"create an binary image for indicate Load neural data\\n    spk_fn = f\\\"{mname}_{datexp}_{blk}_neural_data.npy\\\"\\n    spk_data = np.load(os.path.join(root, 'spk', spk_fn), allow_pickle=True).item()\\n    spk = np.concatenate([s for s in spk_data['spks']], axis=0)\\n    n_neurons, n_frames = spk.shape\\n\\n    # Load retinotopy\\n    ret_fn = f\\\"{mname}_{datexp}_trans.npz\\\"\\n    ret_data = np.load(os.path.join(root, 'retinotopy', ret_fn), allow_pickle=True)\\n    iarea = ret_data['iarea']\\n\\n    # Get valid neuron mask (visual cortex only)\\n    region_idx, valid_mask = get_brain_region_idx(iarea)\\n    valid_neurons = valid_mask\\n\\n    # Get behavior variables\\n    n_trials = beh['ntrials']\\n    corridor_len = beh['Corridor_Length']  # typically 60 dm\\n\\n    # Filter for running frames (VR moving)\\n    ft_move = beh['ft_move'][:n_frames]\\n    vr_moving = ft_move > 0\\n    ft_pos_cum = beh['ft_PosCum'][:n_frames]\\n\\n    # Position-interpolate neural data (matching paper's processing)\\n    interp_spk = position_interpolate_spk(\\n        spk[valid_neurons][:, vr_moving],\\n        ft_pos_cum[vr_moving],\\n        corridor_len,\\n        n_trials,\\n        n_bins=N_POS_BINS\\n    )\\n    # Keep only texture area (first 40 bins)\\n    interp_spk = interp_spk[:, :, :N_TEXTURE_BINS]\\n\\n    # Get running speed per position bin (from behavior data)\\n    run_pos = beh['run_pos']  # (n_trials, 60) - already position-interpolated\\n    run_speed = run_pos[:, :N_TEXTURE_BINS]  # (n_trials, 40)\\n\\n    # Discretize running speed into 4 quartile bins\\n    speed_bins = np.digitize(run_speed, speed_quantile_edges) - 1\\n    speed_bins = np.clip(speed_bins, 0, 3)\\n\\n    # Get lick data per position bin\\n    lick_pos = beh['LickPos']\\n    lick_trind = beh['LickTrind']\\n    lick_binary = lick_to_position_bins(lick_pos, lick_trind, n_trials, N_TEXTURE_BINS)\\n\\n    # position where sound cue was delivered\\n\\n    # Reward availability\\n    is_rew = beh['isRew'].astype(float)\\n\\n    # Position bins for corridor (4 equal 1m bins)\\n    pos_bins = np.zeros(N_TEXTURE_BINS, dtype=int)\\n    for i in range(N_TEXTURE_BINS):\\n        pos_bins[i] = min(i // 10, 3)  # 0-9 -> 0, 10-19 -> 1, 20-29 -> 2, 30-39 -> 3\\n\\n    # Compute day of training for this session\\n    session_date = compute_day_of_training(datexp)\\n\\n    # Build per-trial data\\n    neural_trials = []\\n    input_trials = []\\n    output_trials = []\\n\\n    for tr in range(n_trials):\\n        # Neural: (n_valid_neurons, 40)\\n        neural_trial = interp_spk[:, tr, :].astype(np.float32)\\n\\n        # Input: (4, 40)\\n        # 1. Time to sound cue (seconds) - negative before cue, positive after\\n        time_to_cue = np.array([(i - sound_pos[tr]) * BIN_SIZE_SEC\\n                                 for i in range(N_TEXTURE_BINS)], dtype=np.float32)\\n\\n        # 2. Day of training - broadcast to all time bins\\n        # Will be filled in later with per-mouse relative days\\n        day_val = 0.0  # placeholder\\n        day_of_training = np.full(N_TEXTURE_BINS, day_val, dtype=np.float32)\\n\\n        # 3. Time since trial start (seconds)\\n        time_since_start = np.array([i * BIN_SIZE_SEC for i in range(N_TEXTURE_BINS)],\\n                                     dtype=np.float32)\\n\\n        # 4. Reward availability\\n        reward_avail = np.full(N_TEXTURE_BINS, is_rew[tr], dtype=np.float32)\\n\\n        input_trial = np.stack([time_to_cue, day_of_training, time_since_start, reward_avail],\\n                                axis=0)  # (4, 40)\\n\\n        # Output: (4, 40) - integer categorical values\\n        # 1. Visual stimulus category - broadcast to all time bins\\n        stim_cat = np.full(N_TEXTURE_BINS, stim_indices[tr], dtype=np.int64)\\n\\n        # 2. Licking binary\\n        lick_tr = lick_binary[tr, :].astype(np.int64)\\n\\n        # 3. Position bin\\n        pos_tr = pos_bins.astype(np.int64)\\n\\n        # 4. Running speed bin\\n        speed_tr = speed_bins[tr, :].astype(np.int64)\\n\\n        output_trial = np.stack([stim_cat, lick_tr, pos_tr, speed_tr], axis=0)  # (4, 40)\\n\\n        neural_trials.append(neural_trial)\\n        input_trials.append(input_trial)\\n        output_trials.append(output_trial)\\n\\n    return {\\n        'neural': neural_trials,\\n        'input': input_trials,\\n        'output': output_trials,\\n        'brain_region_idx': region_idx[valid_mask].astype(int),\\n        'n_neurons': valid_mask.sum(),\\n        'n_trials': n_trials,\\n        'mname': mname,\\n        'datexp': datexp,\\n        'session_date': session_date,\\n    }\\n\\n\\ndef main(sample_only=False):\\n    print(\\\"Loading experiment info...\\\")\\n    exp_info = np.load(os.path.join(ROOT, 'beh', 'Imaging_Exp_info.npy'),\\n                       allow_pickle=True).item()\\n\\n    # Collect all unique sessions\\n    print(\\\"Collecting sessions...\\\")\\n    sessions = collect_all_sessions(exp_info, ROOT)\\n    print(f\\\"Found {len(sessions)} unique recording sessions\\\")\\n\\n    # Collect all unique stimulus names across all sessions\\n    all_stim_set = set()\\n    for s in sessions:\\n        for wn in s['beh']['UniqWalls']:\\n            all_stim_set.add(str(wn))\\n    all_stim_names = sorted(all_stim_set)\\n    print(f\\\"Unique stimuli: {all_stim_names}\\\")\\n\\n    # running speed quartiles\\n    ]\\n\\n    # Build the data dict\\n    data = {\\n        'neural': all_neural,\\n        'input': all_input,\\n        'output': all_output,\\n\\n        'subjects': all_subjects,\\n        'subject_idx': np.array(all_subject_idx, dtype=int),\\n\\n        'brain_regions': brain_regions,\\n        'brain_region_idx': all_brain_region_idx,\\n\\n        'input_names': ['time_to_sound_cue', 'day_of_training', 'time_since_trial_start',\\n                        'reward_availability'],\\n        'output_names': ['visual_stimulus', 'licking', 'position', 'running_speed'],\\n        'output_values': output_values,\\n\\n        'metadata': {\\n            'task_description': ('Visual discrimination task in head-fixed mice running through '\\n                                 'linear virtual reality corridors. Total position bins per corridor (paper convention)\\nN_TEXTURE_BINS = 40   # Texture area bins (0-39, = 4m corridor)\\nVR_SPEED = 6.0        # dm/s (60 cm/s)\\nBIN_SIZE_SEC = 1.0 / VR_SPEED  # seconds per position bin = 1/6 s ≈ 0.1667s\\nBIN_SIZE_MS = BIN_SIZE_SEC * 1000  # ≈ 166.67 ms\\n\\n\\ndef position_interpolate_spk(raw_spk, accum_pos, corridor_len, n_trials, n_bins=60):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Position-interpolate spike data to evenly spaced position bins.\\n\\n    Matches utils.spk_pos_interp and utils.get_interpPos_spk from the paper code.\\n    Uses numpy.interp for speed (equivalent to scipy interp1d with extrapolation).\\n\\n    Args:\\n        raw_spk: (n_neurons, n_frames) - neural data for running frames only\\n        accum_pos: (n_frames,) - cumulative position for running frames\\n        corridor_len: corridor length in dm\\n        n_trials: number of trials\\n        n_bins: bins per corridor\\n\\n    Returns:\\n        interp_spk: (n_neurons, n_trials, n_bins)\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    lin_pos = np.arange(0, n_trials, 1.0 / n_bins)\\n    norm_pos = accum_pos / corridor_len\\n    n_neurons = raw_spk.shape[0]\\n    n_target = len(lin_pos)\\n    interp_spk = np.zeros((n_neurons, n_target), dtype=np.float32)\\n\\n    # Use numpy.interp which is much faster than scipy for 1D interpolation\\n    for s in range(n_neurons):\\n        interp_spk[s, :] = np.interp(lin_pos, norm_pos, raw_spk[s, :])\\n\\n    return interp_spk.reshape(n_neurons, n_trials, n_bins)\\n\\n\\ndef get_brain_region_idx(iarea):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Map iarea values to brain region indices.\\n\\n    Brain regions (from paper's neu_area_ID):\\n        V1: iarea == 8\\n        mHV: iarea in {0, 1, 2, 9}\\n        lHV: iarea in {5, 6}\\n        aHV: iarea in {3, 4}\\n\\n    Returns:\\n        region_idx: array of region indices (0=V1, 1=mHV, 2=lHV, 3=aHV)\\n        valid_mask: boolean mask for neurons in visual cortex\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    valid_mask = (iarea != -1) & (iarea != 7)\\n    region_idx = np.full(len(iarea), -1, dtype=int)\\n    region_idx[iarea == 8] = 0  # V1\\n    region_idx[(iarea == 0) | (iarea == 1) | (iarea == 2) | (iarea == 9)] = 1  # mHV\\n    region_idx[(iarea == 5) | (iarea == 6)] = 2  # lHV\\n    region_idx[(iarea == 3) | (iarea == 4)] = 3  # aHV\\n    return region_idx, valid_mask\\n\\n\\ndef lick_to_position_bins(lick_pos, lick_trind, n_trials, n_bins=40):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Convert lick events to binary per-position-bin per-trial.\\n\\n    Args:\\n        lick_pos: position of each lick event (in dm)\\n        lick_trind: trial index of each lick event\\n        n_trials: number of trials\\n        n_bins: number of position bins (texture area)\\n\\n    Returns:\\n        lick_binary: (n_trials, n_bins) binary array\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    lick_binary = np.zeros((n_trials, n_bins), dtype=int)\\n    for i in range(len(lick_pos)):\\n        tr = int(lick_trind[i])\\n        pos = lick_pos[i]\\n        bin_idx = int(pos)\\n        if 0 <= bin_idx < n_bins and 0 <= tr < n_trials:\\n            lick_binary[tr, bin_idx] = 1\\n    return lick_binary\\n\\n\\ndef compute_day_of_training(date_str):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Parse date string like '2022_08_17' to datetime.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    return datetime.strptime(date_str, '%Y_%m_%d')\\n\\n\\ndef collect_all_sessions(exp_info, root):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Collect all unique recording sessions with their metadata.\\n\\n    For recordings appearing in multiple experiment types, use the first one found.\\n    Returns list of session dicts with all needed info.\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    seen_recordings = set()\\n    sessions = []\\n\\n    # Get behavior variables\\n    n_trials = beh['ntrials']\\n    corridor_len = beh['Corridor_Length']  # typically 60 dm\\n\\n    # Filter for running frames (VR moving)\\n    ft_move = beh['ft_move'][:n_frames]\\n    vr_moving = ft_move > 0\\n    ft_pos_cum = beh['ft_PosCum'][:n_frames]\\n\\n    # ≈ 166.67 ms\\n\\n\\ndef position_interpolate_spk(raw_spk, accum_pos, corridor_len, n_trials, n_bins=60):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Position-interpolate spike data to evenly spaced position bins.\\n\\n    Matches utils.spk_pos_interp and utils.get_interpPos_spk from the paper code.\\n    Uses numpy.interp for speed (equivalent to scipy interp1d with extrapolation).\\n\\n    Args:\\n        raw_spk: (n_neurons, n_frames) - neural data for running frames only\\n        accum_pos: (n_frames,) - cumulative position for running frames\\n        corridor_len: corridor length in dm\\n        n_trials: number of trials\\n        n_bins: bins per corridor\\n\\n    Returns:\\n        interp_spk: (n_neurons, n_trials, n_bins)\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    lin_pos = np.arange(0, n_trials, 1.0 / n_bins)\\n    norm_pos = accum_pos / corridor_len\\n    n_neurons = raw_spk.shape[0]\\n    n_target = len(lin_pos)\\n    interp_spk = np.zeros((n_neurons, n_target), dtype=np.float32)\\n\\n    # V1\\n    region_idx[(iarea == 0) | (iarea == 1) | (iarea == 2) | (iarea == 9)] = 1  # mHV\\n    region_idx[(iarea == 5) | (iarea == 6)] = 2  # lHV\\n    region_idx[(iarea == 3) | (iarea == 4)] = 3  # aHV\\n    return region_idx, valid_mask\\n\\n\\ndef lick_to_position_bins(lick_pos, lick_trind, n_trials, n_bins=40):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Convert lick events to binary per-position-bin per-trial.\\n\\n    Args:\\n        lick_pos: position of each lick event (in dm)\\n        lick_trind: trial index of each lick event\\n        n_trials: number of trials\\n        n_bins: number of position bins (texture area)\\n\\n    Returns:\\n        lick_binary: (n_trials, n_bins) binary array\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    lick_binary = np.zeros((n_trials, n_bins), dtype=int)\\n    for i in range(len(lick_pos)):\\n        tr = int(lick_trind[i])\\n        pos = lick_pos[i]\\n        bin_idx = int(pos)\\n        if 0 <= bin_idx < n_bins and 0 <= tr < n_trials:\\n            lick_binary[tr, bin_idx] = 1\\n    return lick_binary\\n\\n\\ndef compute_day_of_training(date_str):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Parse date string like '2022_08_17' to datetime.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    return datetime.strptime(date_str, '%Y_%m_%d')\\n\\n\\ndef collect_all_sessions(exp_info, root):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Collect all unique recording sessions with their metadata.\\n\\n    For recordings appearing in multiple experiment types, use the first one found.\\n    Returns list of session dicts with all needed info.\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    seen_recordings = set()\\n    sessions = []\\n\\n    # Process experiment types in a specific order to prefer more complete annotations\\n    # Prefer test sessions (more stimuli) over train sessions (fewer stimuli)\\n    exp_order = sorted(exp_info.keys(), key=lambda x: (\\n        0 if 'test' in x else 1,  # Reward availability\\n        reward_avail = np.full(N_TEXTURE_BINS, is_rew[tr], dtype=np.float32)\\n\\n        input_trial = np.stack([time_to_cue, day_of_training, time_since_start, reward_avail],\\n                                axis=0)  # (4, 40)\\n\\n        # Output: (4, 40) - integer categorical values\\n        # 1. Sound cue indicates reward zone in '\\n   453→                                 'rewarded corridor.'),\\n   454→            'time_bin_size': BIN_SIZE_MS,\\n   455→            'temporal_alignment_event': 'Trial start (corridor entry)',\\n   456→            'off_start': 0.0,\\n   457→            'off_end': N_TEXTURE_BINS * BIN_SIZE_SEC,\\n   458→            'vr_speed_cm_s': 60.0,\\n   459→            'corridor_length_m': 4.0,\\n   460→            'position_bin_size_dm': 1.0,\\n   461→            'n_position_bins': N_TEXTURE_BINS,\\n   462→            'calcium_indicator': 'GCaMP6s',\\n   463→            'neural_data_type': 'deconvolved fluorescence (Suite2p)',\\n   464→            'frame_rate_hz': 3.17,\\n   465→            'speed_quantile_edges': speed_quantile_edges.tolist(),\\n   466→            'stimulus_names': all_stim_names,\\n   467→            'session_info': session_info_list,\\n   468→            'n_mice': len(all_subjects),\\n   469→            'n_sessions': len(all_neural),\\n   470→            'reference': 'Zhong et al. 2025, Unsupervised pretraining in biological neural networks',\\n   471→        }\\n   472→    }\\n   473→\\n   474→    return data\\n   475→\\n   476→\\n   477→if __name__ == '__main__':\\n   478→    sample_mode = '--sample' in sys.argv\\n   479→\\n   480→    data = main(sample_only=sample_mode)\\n   481→\\n   482→    if sample_mode:\\n   483→        out_path = 'sample_data.pkl'\\n   484→    else:\\n   485→        out_path = 'converted_data.pkl'\\n   486→\\n   487→    print(f\\\"\\\\nSaving to {out_path}...\\\")\\n   488→    with open(out_path, 'wb') as f:\\n   489→        pickle.dump(data, f)\\n   490→    print(f\\\"Saved successfully.\\\")\\n   491→\\n   492→    # Print summary statistics\\n   493→    n_sessions = len(data['neural'])\\n   494→    total_trials = sum(len(data['neural'][i]) for i in range(n_sessions))\\n   495→    total_neurons = sum(data['neural'][i][0].shape[0] for i in range(n_sessions) if len(data['neural'][i]) > 0)\\n   496→    print(f\\\"\\\\nSummary:\\\")\\n   497→    print(f\\\"  Sessions: {n_sessions}\\\")\\n   498→    print(f\\\"  Total trials: {total_trials}\\\")\\n   499→    print(f\\\"  Total neurons (across sessions): {total_neurons}\\\")\\n   500→    print(f\\\"  Subjects: {len(data['subjects'])}\\\")\\n   501→    print(f\\\"  Brain regions: {data['brain_regions']}\\\")\\n   502→    print(f\\\"  Input variables: {data['input_names']}\\\")\\n   503→    print(f\\\"  Output variables: {data['output_names']}\\\")\\n   504→    print(f\\\"  Time bin size: {data['metadata']['time_bin_size']:.2f} ms\\\")\\n   505→    print(f\\\"  Timepoints per trial: {N_TEXTURE_BINS}\\\")\\n   506→\\n\\n[metadata] {\\\"type\\\": \\\"text\\\", \\\"file\\\": {\\\"filePath\\\": \\\"/app/convert_data.py\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\nConvert neural data from Zhong et al. 2025 \\\\\\\"Unsupervised pretraining in biological neural networks\\\\\\\"\\\\ninto the standardized decoder format.\\\\n\\\\nProcessing follows the reference paper and code:\\\\n- Neural data: deconvolved calcium traces from Suite2p, position-interpolated to 60 bins per corridor\\\\n- Only texture area bins (0-39) are used (40 bins = 4m corridor at 1 dm resolution)\\\\n- Only visual cortex neurons are included (iarea != -1 and iarea != 7)\\\\n- Only running frames are used for interpolation (VR moving, ft_move > 0)\\\\n- Brain regions: V1 (iarea=8), mHV (iarea in 0,1,2,9), lHV (iarea in 5,6), aHV (iarea in 3,4)\\\\n\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n\\\\nimport numpy as np\\\\nimport os\\\\nimport pickle\\\\nimport sys\\\\nfrom datetime import datetime\\\\nimport gc\\\\n\\\\nROOT = 'data'\\\\nN_POS_BINS = 60       # Total position bins per corridor (paper convention)\\\\nN_TEXTURE_BINS = 40   # Texture area bins (0-39, = 4m corridor)\\\\nVR_SPEED = 6.0        # dm/s (60 cm/s)\\\\nBIN_SIZE_SEC = 1.0 / VR_SPEED  # seconds per position bin = 1/6 s ≈ 0.1667s\\\\nBIN_SIZE_MS = BIN_SIZE_SEC * 1000  # ≈ 166.67 ms\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef position_interpolate_spk(raw_spk, accum_pos, corridor_len, n_trials, n_bins=60):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Position-interpolate spike data to evenly spaced position bins.\\\\n\\\\n    Matches utils.spk_pos_interp and utils.get_interpPos_spk from the paper code.\\\\n    Uses numpy.interp for speed (equivalent to scipy interp1d with extrapolation).\\\\n\\\\n    Args:\\\\n        raw_spk: (n_neurons, n_frames) - neural data for running frames only\\\\n        accum_pos: (n_frames,) - cumulative position for running frames\\\\n        corridor_len: corridor length in dm\\\\n        n_trials: number of trials\\\\n        n_bins: bins per corridor\\\\n\\\\n    Returns:\\\\n        interp_spk: (n_neurons, n_trials, n_bins)\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    lin_pos = np.arange(0, n_trials, 1.0 / n_bins)\\\\n    norm_pos = accum_pos / corridor_len\\\\n    n_neurons = raw_spk.shape[0]\\\\n    n_target = len(lin_pos)\\\\n    interp_spk = np.zeros((n_neurons, n_target), dtype=np.float32)\\\\n\\\\n    # Use numpy.interp which is much faster than scipy for 1D interpolation\\\\n    for s in range(n_neurons):\\\\n        interp_spk[s, :] = np.interp(lin_pos, norm_pos, raw_spk[s, :])\\\\n\\\\n    return interp_spk.reshape(n_neurons, n_trials, n_bins)\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef get_brain_region_idx(iarea):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Map iarea values to brain region indices.\\\\n\\\\n    Brain regions (from paper's neu_area_ID):\\\\n        V1: iarea == 8\\\\n        mHV: iarea in {0, 1, 2, 9}\\\\n        lHV: iarea in {5, 6}\\\\n        aHV: iarea in {3, 4}\\\\n\\\\n    Returns:\\\\n        region_idx: array of region indices (0=V1, 1=mHV, 2=lHV, 3=aHV)\\\\n        valid_mask: boolean mask for neurons in visual cortex\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    valid_mask = (iarea != -1) & (iarea != 7)\\\\n    region_idx = np.full(len(iarea), -1, dtype=int)\\\\n    region_idx[iarea == 8] = 0  # V1\\\\n    region_idx[(iarea == 0) | (iarea == 1) | (iarea == 2) | (iarea == 9)] = 1  # mHV\\\\n    region_idx[(iarea == 5) | (iarea == 6)] = 2  # lHV\\\\n    region_idx[(iarea == 3) | (iarea == 4)] = 3  # aHV\\\\n    return region_idx, valid_mask\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef lick_to_position_bins(lick_pos, lick_trind, n_trials, n_bins=40):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Convert lick events to binary per-position-bin per-trial.\\\\n\\\\n    Args:\\\\n        lick_pos: position of each lick event (in dm)\\\\n        lick_trind: trial index of each lick event\\\\n        n_trials: number of trials\\\\n        n_bins: number of position bins (texture area)\\\\n\\\\n    Returns:\\\\n        lick_binary: (n_trials, n_bins) binary array\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    lick_binary = np.zeros((n_trials, n_bins), dtype=int)\\\\n    for i in range(len(lick_pos)):\\\\n        tr = int(lick_trind[i])\\\\n        pos = lick_pos[i]\\\\n        bin_idx = int(pos)\\\\n        if 0 <= bin_idx < n_bins and 0 <= tr < n_trials:\\\\n            lick_binary[tr, bin_idx] = 1\\\\n    return lick_binary\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef compute_day_of_training(date_str):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Parse date string like '2022_08_17' to datetime.\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    return datetime.strptime(date_str, '%Y_%m_%d')\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef collect_all_sessions(exp_info, root):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Collect all unique recording sessions with their metadata.\\\\n\\\\n    For recordings appearing in multiple experiment types, use the first one found.\\\\n    Returns list of session dicts with all needed info.\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    seen_recordings = set()\\\\n    sessions = []\\\\n\\\\n    # Process experiment types in a specific order to prefer more complete annotations\\\\n    # Prefer test sessions (more stimuli) over train sessions (fewer stimuli)\\\\n    exp_order = sorted(exp_info.keys(), key=lambda x: (\\\\n        0 if 'test' in x else 1,  # test first\\\\n        0 if 'sup_' in x else 1,  # supervised first (has rewards)\\\\n        0 if 'after' in x else 1,  # after learning first\\\\n        x  # alphabetical tiebreak\\\\n    ))\\\\n\\\\n    for exp_type in exp_order:\\\\n        db_list = exp_info[exp_type]\\\\n        # Load behavior data\\\\n        beh_path = os.path.join(root, 'beh', f'Beh_{exp_type}.npy')\\\\n        if not os.path.exists(beh_path):\\\\n            print(f\\\\\\\"  Warning: behavior file not found for {exp_type}\\\\\\\")\\\\n            continue\\\\n        beh_data = np.load(beh_path, allow_pickle=True).item()\\\\n\\\\n        for ndb in db_list:\\\\n            rec_key = (ndb['mname'], ndb['datexp'], ndb['blk'])\\\\n            if rec_key in seen_recordings:\\\\n                continue\\\\n            seen_recordings.add(rec_key)\\\\n\\\\n            # Build behavior key\\\\n            stimtype = ndb.get('stimtype', '')\\\\n            if stimtype:\\\\n                beh_key = f\\\\\\\"{ndb['mname']}_{ndb['datexp']}_{ndb['blk']}_{stimtype}\\\\\\\"\\\\n            else:\\\\n                beh_key = f\\\\\\\"{ndb['mname']}_{ndb['datexp']}_{ndb['blk']}\\\\\\\"\\\\n\\\\n            if beh_key not in beh_data:\\\\n                print(f\\\\\\\"  Warning: behavior key {beh_key} not found in {exp_type}\\\\\\\")\\\\n                continue\\\\n\\\\n            sessions.append({\\\\n                'mname': ndb['mname'],\\\\n                'datexp': ndb['datexp'],\\\\n                'blk': ndb['blk'],\\\\n                'exp_type': exp_type,\\\\n                'beh_key': beh_key,\\\\n                'beh': beh_data[beh_key],\\\\n                'ndb': ndb,\\\\n            })\\\\n\\\\n    return sessions\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef process_session(session_info, root, all_stim_names, speed_quantile_edges):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Process a single recording session into decoder format.\\\\n\\\\n    Args:\\\\n        session_info: dict with session metadata and behavior\\\\n        root: data root directory\\\\n        all_stim_names: list of all unique stimulus names (for consistent labeling)\\\\n        speed_quantile_edges: pre-computed quartile edges for running speed\\\\n\\\\n    Returns:\\\\n        dict with neural, input, output, brain_region_idx for this session\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    ndb = session_info['ndb']\\\\n    beh = session_info['beh']\\\\n    mname = ndb['mname']\\\\n    datexp = ndb['datexp']\\\\n    blk = ndb['blk']\\\\n\\\\n    # Load neural data\\\\n    spk_fn = f\\\\\\\"{mname}_{datexp}_{blk}_neural_data.npy\\\\\\\"\\\\n    spk_data = np.load(os.path.join(root, 'spk', spk_fn), allow_pickle=True).item()\\\\n    spk = np.concatenate([s for s in spk_data['spks']], axis=0)\\\\n    del spk_data\\\\n    n_neurons, n_frames = spk.shape\\\\n\\\\n    # Load retinotopy\\\\n    ret_fn = f\\\\\\\"{mname}_{datexp}_trans.npz\\\\\\\"\\\\n    ret_data = np.load(os.path.join(root, 'retinotopy', ret_fn), allow_pickle=True)\\\\n    iarea = ret_data['iarea']\\\\n\\\\n    # Get valid neuron mask (visual cortex only)\\\\n    region_idx, valid_mask = get_brain_region_idx(iarea)\\\\n    valid_neurons = valid_mask\\\\n\\\\n    # Get behavior variables\\\\n    n_trials = beh['ntrials']\\\\n    corridor_len = beh['Corridor_Length']  # typically 60 dm\\\\n\\\\n    # Filter for running frames (VR moving)\\\\n    ft_move = beh['ft_move'][:n_frames]\\\\n    vr_moving = ft_move > 0\\\\n    ft_pos_cum = beh['ft_PosCum'][:n_frames]\\\\n\\\\n    # Position-interpolate neural data (matching paper's processing)\\\\n    # Only pass valid (visual cortex) neurons and running frames\\\\n    valid_spk = spk[valid_neurons][:, vr_moving]\\\\n    del spk  # free memory\\\\n    interp_spk = position_interpolate_spk(\\\\n        valid_spk,\\\\n        ft_pos_cum[vr_moving],\\\\n        corridor_len,\\\\n        n_trials,\\\\n        n_bins=N_POS_BINS\\\\n    )\\\\n    del valid_spk  # free memory\\\\n    # Keep only texture area (first 40 bins)\\\\n    interp_spk = interp_spk[:, :, :N_TEXTURE_BINS]\\\\n\\\\n    # Get running speed per position bin (from behavior data)\\\\n    run_pos = beh['run_pos']  # (n_trials, 60) - already position-interpolated\\\\n    run_speed = run_pos[:, :N_TEXTURE_BINS]  # (n_trials, 40)\\\\n\\\\n    # Discretize running speed into 4 quartile bins\\\\n    # np.digitize with 3 edges (Q25, Q50, Q75) returns 0-3 directly\\\\n    speed_bins = np.digitize(run_speed, speed_quantile_edges)\\\\n    speed_bins = np.clip(speed_bins, 0, 3)\\\\n\\\\n    # Get lick data per position bin\\\\n    lick_pos = beh['LickPos']\\\\n    lick_trind = beh['LickTrind']\\\\n    lick_binary = lick_to_position_bins(lick_pos, lick_trind, n_trials, N_TEXTURE_BINS)\\\\n\\\\n    # Get stimulus names per trial\\\\n    wall_names = beh['WallName']\\\\n\\\\n    # Map stimulus names to indices\\\\n    stim_indices = np.array([all_stim_names.index(wn) for wn in wall_names])\\\\n\\\\n    # Get sound cue position (in dm within corridor)\\\\n    sound_pos = beh['SoundPos']  # position where sound cue was delivered\\\\n\\\\n    # Reward availability\\\\n    is_rew = beh['isRew'].astype(float)\\\\n\\\\n    # Position bins for corridor (4 equal 1m bins)\\\\n    pos_bins = np.zeros(N_TEXTURE_BINS, dtype=int)\\\\n    for i in range(N_TEXTURE_BINS):\\\\n        pos_bins[i] = min(i // 10, 3)  # 0-9 -> 0, 10-19 -> 1, 20-29 -> 2, 30-39 -> 3\\\\n\\\\n    # Compute day of training for this session\\\\n    session_date = compute_day_of_training(datexp)\\\\n\\\\n    # Build per-trial data\\\\n    neural_trials = []\\\\n    input_trials = []\\\\n    output_trials = []\\\\n\\\\n    for tr in range(n_trials):\\\\n        # Neural: (n_valid_neurons, 40)\\\\n        neural_trial = interp_spk[:, tr, :].astype(np.float32)\\\\n\\\\n        # Input: (4, 40)\\\\n        # 1. Time to sound cue (seconds) - negative before cue, positive after\\\\n        time_to_cue = np.array([(i - sound_pos[tr]) * BIN_SIZE_SEC\\\\n                                 for i in range(N_TEXTURE_BINS)], dtype=np.float32)\\\\n\\\\n        # 2. Day of training - broadcast to all time bins\\\\n        # Will be filled in later with per-mouse relative days\\\\n        day_val = 0.0  # placeholder\\\\n        day_of_training = np.full(N_TEXTURE_BINS, day_val, dtype=np.float32)\\\\n\\\\n        # 3. Time since trial start (seconds)\\\\n        time_since_start = np.array([i * BIN_SIZE_SEC for i in range(N_TEXTURE_BINS)],\\\\n                                     dtype=np.float32)\\\\n\\\\n        # 4. Reward availability\\\\n        reward_avail = np.full(N_TEXTURE_BINS, is_rew[tr], dtype=np.float32)\\\\n\\\\n        input_trial = np.stack([time_to_cue, day_of_training, time_since_start, reward_avail],\\\\n                                axis=0)  # (4, 40)\\\\n\\\\n        # Output: (4, 40) - integer categorical values\\\\n        # 1. Visual stimulus category - broadcast to all time bins\\\\n        stim_cat = np.full(N_TEXTURE_BINS, stim_indices[tr], dtype=np.int64)\\\\n\\\\n        # 2. Licking binary\\\\n        lick_tr = lick_binary[tr, :].astype(np.int64)\\\\n\\\\n        # 3. Position bin\\\\n        pos_tr = pos_bins.astype(np.int64)\\\\n\\\\n        # 4. Running speed bin\\\\n        speed_tr = speed_bins[tr, :].astype(np.int64)\\\\n\\\\n        output_trial = np.stack([stim_cat, lick_tr, pos_tr, speed_tr], axis=0)  # (4, 40)\\\\n\\\\n        neural_trials.append(neural_trial)\\\\n        input_trials.append(input_trial)\\\\n        output_trials.append(output_trial)\\\\n\\\\n    return {\\\\n        'neural': neural_trials,\\\\n        'input': input_trials,\\\\n        'output': output_trials,\\\\n        'brain_region_idx': region_idx[valid_mask].astype(int),\\\\n        'n_neurons': valid_mask.sum(),\\\\n        'n_trials': n_trials,\\\\n        'mname': mname,\\\\n        'datexp': datexp,\\\\n        'session_date': session_date,\\\\n    }\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef main(sample_only=False):\\\\n    print(\\\\\\\"Loading experiment info...\\\\\\\")\\\\n    exp_info = np.load(os.path.join(ROOT, 'beh', 'Imaging_Exp_info.npy'),\\\\n                       allow_pickle=True).item()\\\\n\\\\n    # Collect all unique sessions\\\\n    print(\\\\\\\"Collecting sessions...\\\\\\\")\\\\n    sessions = collect_all_sessions(exp_info, ROOT)\\\\n    print(f\\\\\\\"Found {len(sessions)} unique recording sessions\\\\\\\")\\\\n\\\\n    # Collect all unique stimulus names across all sessions\\\\n    all_stim_set = set()\\\\n    for s in sessions:\\\\n        for wn in s['beh']['UniqWalls']:\\\\n            all_stim_set.add(str(wn))\\\\n    all_stim_names = sorted(all_stim_set)\\\\n    print(f\\\\\\\"Unique stimuli: {all_stim_names}\\\\\\\")\\\\n\\\\n    # Collect all unique subjects\\\\n    all_subjects = sorted(set(s['mname'] for s in sessions))\\\\n    print(f\\\\\\\"Unique subjects: {all_subjects}\\\\\\\")\\\\n\\\\n    # Compute running speed quantile edges across all sessions\\\\n    print(\\\\\\\"Computing running speed quantiles...\\\\\\\")\\\\n    all_speeds = []\\\\n    for s in sessions:\\\\n        run_pos = s['beh']['run_pos'][:, :N_TEXTURE_BINS]\\\\n        all_speeds.append(run_pos.ravel())\\\\n    all_speeds = np.concatenate(all_speeds)\\\\n    speed_quantile_edges = np.percentile(all_speeds, [25, 50, 75])\\\\n    print(f\\\\\\\"Running speed quartile edges: {speed_quantile_edges}\\\\\\\")\\\\n    del all_speeds\\\\n\\\\n    # Compute day of training for each session (relative to first recording per mouse)\\\\n    mouse_first_date = {}\\\\n    for s in sessions:\\\\n        d = compute_day_of_training(s['datexp'])\\\\n        if s['mname'] not in mouse_first_date or d < mouse_first_date[s['mname']]:\\\\n            mouse_first_date[s['mname']] = d\\\\n\\\\n    session_days = {}\\\\n    for s in sessions:\\\\n        d = compute_day_of_training(s['datexp'])\\\\n        days = (d - mouse_first_date[s['mname']]).days\\\\n        key = (s['mname'], s['datexp'], s['blk'])\\\\n        session_days[key] = float(days)\\\\n\\\\n    if sample_only:\\\\n        # Use first 3 sessions for sample\\\\n        sessions = sessions[:3]\\\\n        print(f\\\\\\\"Sample mode: using {len(sessions)} sessions\\\\\\\")\\\\n\\\\n    # Process each session\\\\n    brain_regions = ['V1', 'mHV', 'lHV', 'aHV']\\\\n\\\\n    all_neural = []\\\\n    all_input = []\\\\n    all_output = []\\\\n    all_brain_region_idx = []\\\\n    all_subject_idx = []\\\\n    session_info_list = []\\\\n\\\\n    for i, s in enumerate(sessions):\\\\n        rec_key = (s['mname'], s['datexp'], s['blk'])\\\\n        print(f\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\nProcessing session {i+1}/{len(sessions)}: {rec_key} ({s['exp_type']})\\\\\\\")\\\\n\\\\n        try:\\\\n            result = process_session(s, ROOT, all_stim_names, speed_quantile_edges)\\\\n        except Exception as e:\\\\n            print(f\\\\\\\"  ERROR processing session: {e}\\\\\\\")\\\\n            import traceback\\\\n            traceback.print_exc()\\\\n            continue\\\\n\\\\n        # Fill in day_of_training\\\\n        day_val = session_days[rec_key]\\\\n        for trial_input in result['input']:\\\\n            trial_input[1, :] = day_val  # row 1 = day_of_training\\\\n\\\\n        # Check minimum trials\\\\n        if result['n_trials'] < 2:\\\\n            print(f\\\\\\\"  Skipping: only {result['n_trials']} trials\\\\\\\")\\\\n            continue\\\\n\\\\n        all_neural.append(result['neural'])\\\\n        all_input.append(result['input'])\\\\n        all_output.append(result['output'])\\\\n        all_brain_region_idx.append(result['brain_region_idx'])\\\\n        all_subject_idx.append(all_subjects.index(result['mname']))\\\\n\\\\n        session_info_list.append({\\\\n            'mname': s['mname'],\\\\n            'datexp': s['datexp'],\\\\n            'blk': s['blk'],\\\\n            'exp_type': s['exp_type'],\\\\n            'n_neurons': result['n_neurons'],\\\\n            'n_trials': result['n_trials'],\\\\n            'day_of_training': day_val,\\\\n        })\\\\n\\\\n        print(f\\\\\\\"  Neurons: {result['n_neurons']}, Trials: {result['n_trials']}, \\\\\\\"\\\\n              f\\\\\\\"Day: {day_val}\\\\\\\")\\\\n        gc.collect()\\\\n\\\\n    print(f\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n{'='*60}\\\\\\\")\\\\n    print(f\\\\\\\"Total sessions processed: {len(all_neural)}\\\\\\\")\\\\n    print(f\\\\\\\"Total subjects: {len(all_subjects)}\\\\\\\")\\\\n\\\\n    # Build output_values\\\\n    output_values = [\\\\n        all_stim_names,  # visual stimulus categories\\\\n        ['no_lick', 'lick'],  # licking\\\\n        ['0-1m', '1-2m', '2-3m', '3-4m'],  # position bins\\\\n        ['Q1', 'Q2', 'Q3', 'Q4'],  # running speed quartiles\\\\n    ]\\\\n\\\\n    # Build the data dict\\\\n    data = {\\\\n        'neural': all_neural,\\\\n        'input': all_input,\\\\n        'output': all_output,\\\\n\\\\n        'subjects': all_subjects,\\\\n        'subject_idx': np.array(all_subject_idx, dtype=int),\\\\n\\\\n        'brain_regions': brain_regions,\\\\n        'brain_region_idx': all_brain_region_idx,\\\\n\\\\n        'input_names': ['time_to_sound_cue', 'day_of_training', 'time_since_trial_start',\\\\n                        'reward_availability'],\\\\n        'output_names': ['visual_stimulus', 'licking', 'position', 'running_speed'],\\\\n        'output_values': output_values,\\\\n\\\\n        'metadata': {\\\\n            'task_description': ('Visual discrimination task in head-fixed mice running through '\\\\n                                 'linear virtual reality corridors. Total position bins per corridor (paper convention)\\nN_TEXTURE_BINS = 40   # Texture area bins (0-39, = 4m corridor)\\nVR_SPEED = 6.0        # dm/s (60 cm/s)\\nBIN_SIZE_SEC = 1.0 / VR_SPEED  # seconds per position bin = 1/6 s ≈ 0.1667s\\nBIN_SIZE_MS = BIN_SIZE_SEC * 1000  # ≈ 166.67 ms\\n\\n\\ndef position_interpolate_spk(raw_spk, accum_pos, corridor_len, n_trials, n_bins=60):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Position-interpolate spike data to evenly spaced position bins.\\n\\n    Matches utils.spk_pos_interp and utils.get_interpPos_spk from the paper code.\\n    Uses numpy.interp for speed (equivalent to scipy interp1d with extrapolation).\\n\\n    Args:\\n        raw_spk: (n_neurons, n_frames) - neural data for running frames only\\n        accum_pos: (n_frames,) - cumulative position for running frames\\n        corridor_len: corridor length in dm\\n        n_trials: number of trials\\n        n_bins: bins per corridor\\n\\n    Returns:\\n        interp_spk: (n_neurons, n_trials, n_bins)\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    lin_pos = np.arange(0, n_trials, 1.0 / n_bins)\\n    norm_pos = accum_pos / corridor_len\\n    n_neurons = raw_spk.shape[0]\\n    n_target = len(lin_pos)\\n    interp_spk = np.zeros((n_neurons, n_target), dtype=np.float32)\\n\\n    # Use numpy.interp which is much faster than scipy for 1D interpolation\\n    for s in range(n_neurons):\\n        interp_spk[s, :] = np.interp(lin_pos, norm_pos, raw_spk[s, :])\\n\\n    return interp_spk.reshape(n_neurons, n_trials, n_bins)\\n\\n\\ndef get_brain_region_idx(iarea):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Map iarea values to brain region indices.\\n\\n    Brain regions (from paper's neu_area_ID):\\n        V1: iarea == 8\\n        mHV: iarea in {0, 1, 2, 9}\\n        lHV: iarea in {5, 6}\\n        aHV: iarea in {3, 4}\\n\\n    Returns:\\n        region_idx: array of region indices (0=V1, 1=mHV, 2=lHV, 3=aHV)\\n        valid_mask: boolean mask for neurons in visual cortex\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    valid_mask = (iarea != -1) & (iarea != 7)\\n    region_idx = np.full(len(iarea), -1, dtype=int)\\n    region_idx[iarea == 8] = 0  # V1\\n    region_idx[(iarea == 0) | (iarea == 1) | (iarea == 2) | (iarea == 9)] = 1  # mHV\\n    region_idx[(iarea == 5) | (iarea == 6)] = 2  # lHV\\n    region_idx[(iarea == 3) | (iarea == 4)] = 3  # aHV\\n    return region_idx, valid_mask\\n\\n\\ndef lick_to_position_bins(lick_pos, lick_trind, n_trials, n_bins=40):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Convert lick events to binary per-position-bin per-trial.\\n\\n    Args:\\n        lick_pos: position of each lick event (in dm)\\n        lick_trind: trial index of each lick event\\n        n_trials: number of trials\\n        n_bins: number of position bins (texture area)\\n\\n    Returns:\\n        lick_binary: (n_trials, n_bins) binary array\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    lick_binary = np.zeros((n_trials, n_bins), dtype=int)\\n    for i in range(len(lick_pos)):\\n        tr = int(lick_trind[i])\\n        pos = lick_pos[i]\\n        bin_idx = int(pos)\\n        if 0 <= bin_idx < n_bins and 0 <= tr < n_trials:\\n            lick_binary[tr, bin_idx] = 1\\n    return lick_binary\\n\\n\\ndef compute_day_of_training(date_str):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Parse date string like '2022_08_17' to datetime.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    return datetime.strptime(date_str, '%Y_%m_%d')\\n\\n\\ndef collect_all_sessions(exp_info, root):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Collect all unique recording sessions with their metadata.\\n\\n    For recordings appearing in multiple experiment types, use the first one found.\\n    Returns list of session dicts with all needed info.\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    seen_recordings = set()\\n    sessions = []\\n\\n    # Process experiment types in a specific order to prefer more complete annotations\\n    # Prefer test sessions (more stimuli) over train sessions (fewer stimuli)\\n    exp_order = sorted(exp_info.keys(), key=lambda x: (\\n        0 if 'test' in x else 1,  # Load behavior data\\n        beh_path = os.path.join(root, 'beh', f'Beh_{exp_type}.npy')\\n        if not os.path.exists(beh_path):\\n            print(f\\\"  Warning: behavior file not found for {exp_type}\\\")\\n            continue\\n        beh_data = np.load(beh_path, allow_pickle=True).item()\\n\\n        for ndb in db_list:\\n            rec_key = (ndb['mname'], ndb['datexp'], ndb['blk'])\\n            if rec_key in seen_recordings:\\n                continue\\n            seen_recordings.add(rec_key)\\n\\n            # Build behavior key\\n            stimtype = ndb.get('stimtype', '')\\n            if stimtype:\\n                beh_key = f\\\"{ndb['mname']}_{ndb['datexp']}_{ndb['blk']}_{stimtype}\\\"\\n            else:\\n                beh_key = f\\\"{ndb['mname']}_{ndb['datexp']}_{ndb['blk']}\\\"\\n\\n            if beh_key not in beh_data:\\n                print(f\\\"  Warning: behavior key {beh_key} not found in {exp_type}\\\")\\n                continue\\n\\n            sessions.append({\\n                'mname': ndb['mname'],\\n                'datexp': ndb['datexp'],\\n                'blk': ndb['blk'],\\n                'exp_type': exp_type,\\n                'beh_key': beh_key,\\n                'beh': beh_data[beh_key],\\n                'ndb': ndb,\\n            })\\n\\n    return sessions\\n\\n\\ndef process_session(session_info, root, all_stim_names, speed_quantile_edges):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Process a single recording session into decoder format.\\n\\n    Args:\\n        session_info: dict with session metadata and behavior\\n        root: data root directory\\n        all_stim_names: list of all unique stimulus names (for consistent labeling)\\n        speed_quantile_edges: pre-computed quartile edges for running speed\\n\\n    Returns:\\n        dict with neural, input, output, brain_region_idx for this session\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    ndb = session_info['ndb']\\n    beh = session_info['beh']\\n    mname = ndb['mname']\\n    datexp = ndb['datexp']\\n    blk = ndb['blk']\\n\\n    # Load retinotopy\\n    ret_fn = f\\\"{mname}_{datexp}_trans.npz\\\"\\n    ret_data = np.load(os.path.join(root, 'retinotopy', ret_fn), allow_pickle=True)\\n    iarea = ret_data['iarea']\\n\\n    # Get valid neuron mask (visual cortex only)\\n    region_idx, valid_mask = get_brain_region_idx(iarea)\\n    valid_neurons = valid_mask\\n\\n    # Get behavior variables\\n    n_trials = beh['ntrials']\\n    corridor_len = beh['Corridor_Length']  # typically 60 dm\\n\\n    # Filter for running frames (VR moving)\\n    ft_move = beh['ft_move'][:n_frames]\\n    vr_moving = ft_move > 0\\n    ft_pos_cum = beh['ft_PosCum'][:n_frames]\\n\\n    # Position-interpolate neural data (matching paper's processing)\\n    # Only pass valid (visual cortex) neurons and running frames\\n    valid_spk = spk[valid_neurons][:, vr_moving]\\n    del spk  # free memory\\n    interp_spk = position_interpolate_spk(\\n        valid_spk,\\n        ft_pos_cum[vr_moving],\\n        corridor_len,\\n        n_trials,\\n        n_bins=N_POS_BINS\\n    )\\n    del valid_spk  # 0-9 -> 0, 10-19 -> 1, 20-29 -> 2, 30-39 -> 3\\n\\n    # Compute day of training for this session\\n    session_date = compute_day_of_training(datexp)\\n\\n    # Build per-trial data\\n    neural_trials = []\\n    input_trials = []\\n    output_trials = []\\n\\n    for tr in range(n_trials):\\n        # Day of training - broadcast to all time bins\\n        # Will be filled in later with per-mouse relative days\\n        day_val = 0.0  # placeholder\\n        day_of_training = np.full(N_TEXTURE_BINS, day_val, dtype=np.float32)\\n\\n        # 3. Time since trial start (seconds)\\n        time_since_start = np.array([i * BIN_SIZE_SEC for i in range(N_TEXTURE_BINS)],\\n                                     dtype=np.float32)\\n\\n        # 4. Reward availability\\n        reward_avail = np.full(N_TEXTURE_BINS, is_rew[tr], dtype=np.float32)\\n\\n        input_trial = np.stack([time_to_cue, day_of_training, time_since_start, reward_avail],\\n                                axis=0)  # (4, 40)\\n\\n        # Output: (4, 40) - integer categorical values\\n        # 1. Visual stimulus category - broadcast to all time bins\\n        stim_cat = np.full(N_TEXTURE_BINS, stim_indices[tr], dtype=np.int64)\\n\\n        # 2. Collect all unique sessions\\n    print(\\\"Collecting sessions...\\\")\\n    sessions = collect_all_sessions(exp_info, ROOT)\\n    print(f\\\"Found {len(sessions)} unique recording sessions\\\")\\n\\n    # Collect all unique stimulus names across all sessions\\n    all_stim_set = set()\\n    for s in sessions:\\n        for wn in s['beh']['UniqWalls']:\\n            all_stim_set.add(str(wn))\\n    all_stim_names = sorted(all_stim_set)\\n    print(f\\\"Unique stimuli: {all_stim_names}\\\")\\n\\n    # Compute day of training for each session (relative to first recording per mouse)\\n    mouse_first_date = {}\\n    for s in sessions:\\n        d = compute_day_of_training(s['datexp'])\\n        if s['mname'] not in mouse_first_date or d < mouse_first_date[s['mname']]:\\n            mouse_first_date[s['mname']] = d\\n\\n    session_days = {}\\n    for s in sessions:\\n        d = compute_day_of_training(s['datexp'])\\n        days = (d - mouse_first_date[s['mname']]).days\\n        key = (s['mname'], s['datexp'], s['blk'])\\n        session_days[key] = float(days)\\n\\n    if sample_only:\\n        # correction, spike deconvolution with tau=0.75s)\\n\\n## Processing Decisions\\n\\n### Neural Data\\n- **Position interpolation**: Neural activity is interpolated from frame-by-frame data to evenly-spaced position bins (60 bins per 6m corridor), following `spk_pos_interp()` / `get_interpPos_spk()` from `code/utils.py`.\\n- **Texture area only**: Only the first 40 bins (4m texture corridor) are used; the 20 bins of grey space between corridors are excluded.\\n- **Running frames only**: Only frames where the VR was moving (`ft_move > 0`) are used for interpolation, matching the paper's approach of excluding stationary periods.\\n- **Neuron filtering**: Only visual cortex neurons are included (iarea != -1 and iarea != 7), following `load_retino()` and `neu_area_ID()` from `code/utils.py`.\\n- **Interpolation method**: `numpy.interp` is used instead of `scipy.interpolate.interp1d` for speed (equivalent results for 1D linear interpolation).\\n\\n### Brain Regions\\nFollowing `neu_area_ID()` from `code/utils.py`:\\n- **V1**: iarea == 8\\n- **mHV** (medial higher visual): iarea in {0, 1, 2, 9}\\n- **lHV** (lateral higher visual): iarea in {5, 6}\\n- **aHV** (anterior higher visual): iarea in {3, 4}\\n- Excluded: iarea == -1 (not in visual cortex) and iarea == 7 (undefined region)\\n\\n### Temporal Alignment\\n- **Alignment event**: Trial start (corridor entry)\\n- **Time bin size**: 1 dm / 6 dm/s = 166.67 ms\\n- **Timepoints per trial**: 40 (= 4m corridor at 1 dm resolution)\\n- **VR speed**: Constant 60 cm/s (6 dm/s) when mouse runs above 6 cm/s threshold\\n\\n### Decoder Inputs\\n1. **time_to_sound_cue**: Continuous, time-varying. Computed as (position_bin - sound_cue_position) * bin_size_sec. Negative before cue, positive after. Sound cue position from `beh['SoundPos']`.\\n2. **day_of_training**: Continuous, constant within trial. Days since first recording for each mouse.\\n3. **time_since_trial_start**: Continuous, time-varying. Linear from 0 to ~6.5 seconds across 40 bins.\\n4. **reward_availability**: Binary, per-trial. 1 if rewarded corridor, 0 otherwise. From `beh['isRew']`.\\n\\n### Decoder Outputs\\n1. **visual_stimulus**: Categorical, per-trial (broadcast across time bins). 15 unique stimuli: circle1/2/3, leaf1/2/3, leaf1_swap1/2, rock1/2, wood1/2/5, wood1_swap1/2. Mapped to integer indices 0-14.\\n2. **licking**: Binary, time-varying. 1 if any lick event occurred in that position bin, 0 otherwise. Derived from `beh['LickPos']` and `beh['LickTrind']`.\\n3. **position**: 4 bins (0-3), time-varying. Each bin covers 1m of corridor (bins 0-9 -> position 0, 10-19 -> position 1, etc.).\\n4. **running_speed**: 4 quartile bins (0-3), time-varying. Quartile edges computed globally across all sessions using `beh['run_pos']`. Edges: [16.58, 28.72, 43.29] cm/s.\\n\\n### Session Selection\\n- 23 experiment types in `Imaging_Exp_info.npy`, containing recordings that can overlap across types.\\n- Unique recordings identified by (mname, datexp, blk) tuple.\\n- When a recording appears in multiple experiment types, the first match is used, with preference ordering: test > non-test, supervised > unsupervised, after-learning > before-learning.\\n- All 89 unique recordings have corresponding neural data and retinotopy files.\\n\\n### Running Speed Binning\\n- Quartile edges computed across all 89 sessions' `run_pos` data (40 texture bins per trial).\\n- `np.digitize(speed, edges)` with 3 quartile edges returns values 0-3 directly (0 = below Q25, 1 = Q25-Q50, 2 = Q50-Q75, 3 = above Q75).\\n\\n## Sanity Checks\\n\\n### Paper Consistency\\n- **89 recordings in 19 mice**: Matches paper's \\\"We performed 89 recordings in 19 mice\\\" (Methods).\\n- **Neuron counts**: Range 17,363 to 78,815 per session. Paper states \\\"20,547 to 89,577 neurons in each recording\\\" (before neuron filtering by visual cortex).\\n- **Brain regions**: V1 has the most neurons (1,833,035), consistent with V1 being the largest visual area.\\n- **Position bins**: 40 bins at 1 dm each = 4m corridor, matching \\\"corridors were each 4 m long\\\".\\n- **Sound cue range**: Input time_to_sound_cue ranges approximately [-6.5, 6.3] seconds, consistent with sound cue uniformly distributed between 0.5m and 3.5m.\\n- **Licking**: Only present in supervised sessions (sessions 1-15 and 53-61, 77-80), matching that unsupervised/naive mice were not water restricted.\\n- **Reward availability**: Only 1 in supervised sessions, 0 in all unsupervised/naive/grating sessions.\\n\\n### Data Format Validation\\n- `verify_data_format()` passes with no errors or warnings.\\n- All trials have consistent dimensions: neural (n_neurons, 40), input (4, 40), output (4, 40).\\n- Output values are all integers in expected ranges.\\n- Position output has exactly 25% per bin (by construction).\\n- Running speed shows all 4 quartile bins (0-3) with expected ~25% overall distribution.\\n\\n### Decoder Performance (Sample: 3 sessions)\\n- **visual_stimulus**: 0.94 balanced accuracy (chance: 0.07)\\n- **licking**: 0.69 balanced accuracy (chance: 0.50)\\n- **position**: 0.78 balanced accuracy (chance: 0.25)\\n- **running_speed**: 0.43 balanced accuracy (chance: 0.25)\\n\\nAll outputs decode well above chance, indicating neural data properly encodes these variables.\\n\\n## Files Generated\\n- Quartile edges computed globally across all sessions using `beh['run_pos']`. Edges: [16.58, 28.72, 43.29] cm/s.\\n\\n### Session Selection\\n- 23 experiment types in `Imaging_Exp_info.npy`, containing recordings that can overlap across types.\\n- Unique recordings identified by (mname, datexp, blk) tuple.\\n- When a recording appears in multiple experiment types, the first match is used, with preference ordering: test > non-test, supervised > unsupervised, after-learning > before-learning.\\n- All 89 unique recordings have corresponding neural data and retinotopy files.\\n\\n### Running Speed Binning\\n- Quartile edges computed across all 89 sessions' `run_pos` data (40 texture bins per trial).\\n- `np.digitize(speed, edges)` with 3 quartile edges returns values 0-3 directly (0 = below Q25, 1 = Q25-Q50, 2 = Q50-Q75, 3 = above Q75).\\n\\n## Sanity Checks\\n\\n### Paper Consistency\\n- **89 recordings in 19 mice**: Matches paper's \\\"We performed 89 recordings in 19 mice\\\" (Methods).\\n- **Neuron counts**: Range 17,363 to 78,815 per session. largest visual area.\\n- **Position bins**: 40 bins at 1 dm each = 4m corridor, matching \\\"corridors were each 4 m long\\\".\\n- **Sound cue range**: Input time_to_sound_cue ranges approximately [-6.5, 6.3] seconds, consistent with sound cue uniformly distributed between 0.5m and 3.5m.\\n- **Licking**: Only present in supervised sessions (sessions 1-15 and 53-61, 77-80), matching that 375→\\n   376→def get_dist_img(xpos, ypos, sel_idx=None, sig=30, sig_bg=30, xoff=800, yoff=800):\\n   377→    from scipy import ndimage\\n   378→    \\\"\\\"\\\"create an binary image for indicate 375→\\n   376→def get_dist_img(xpos, ypos, sel_idx=None, sig=30, sig_bg=30, xoff=800, yoff=800):\\n   377→    from scipy import ndimage\\n   378→    \\\"\\\"\\\"create an binary image for indicate Mice had to discriminate between visual texture patterns in two corridors; these corridors were repeated in pseudo-random order. The visual patterns in each corridor were obtained as ‘frozen’ crops from large photographs of naturalistic textures. For simplicity, we denote the stimuli as ‘leaf’ and ‘circle’, even though other visual stimuli were also used in some mice (‘rock’ and ‘bricks’; see Methods and Extended Data Fig. 1a). The visual stimuli were spatial frequency matched between categories to encourage the use of higher-order visual features in discrimination. A sound cue was presented at a random position inside each corridor and was followed by the availability of water in rewarded trials only (Fig. 1a). After approximately 2 weeks of training (Fig. 1b), mice demonstrated selective licking in the rewarded corridor in anticipation of reward delivery (Fig. 1c,d; error bars on all figures represent s.e.m.). After learning, we introduced unrewarded test stimuli ‘leaf2’ and ‘circle2’, which were different frozen crops of the same photographs. We then continued training with unrewarded leaf2 until the mice stopped licking to this stimulus, at which point we introduced another test stimulus (‘leaf3’) as well as spatially shuffled versions of leaf1 (Fig. 1b).\\n     2→\\n     3→Mice in the unsupervised cohort also ran through the same corridors for similar periods of time, but did not receive water rewards and were not water restricted. We also studied a cohort of mice that ran through a virtual reality corridor with gratings on the walls. These served as a control to show the effect of simple exposure to virtual reality, independent of the image patterns shown. To ensure that all mice had a comparable visual experience, we fixed the speed of the virtual reality when mice ran faster than a speed threshold, and kept the virtual reality stationary otherwise. The overall running speeds were similar before and after learning, and between the task and unsupervised cohorts (Extended Data Fig. 2). We only considered timepoints during running for analysis, which removed time periods when the task mice stopped to collect water rewards.\\n     4→\\n     5→Before and after learning, we recorded from large neural populations across many visual areas simultaneously using a two-photon mesoscope (Fig. 1e). We ran Suite2p on this data to obtain the activity traces from 20,547 to 89,577 neurons in each recording.\\n     6→\\n     7→It is possible that the neural plasticity that we observed was due to spatial learning and navigation signals, which have been found to modulate firing rates even in the visual cortex. Alternatively, the neural plasticity might be due to adaptation to the visual statistics of the natural images that we presented. To present the stimuli, we used PsychToolbox-3 in MATLAB. The virtual reality corridors were each 4 m long, with 2 m of grey space between corridors. The corridors were shown in a random order. The mice moved forward in the virtual reality corridors by running faster than a threshold of 6 cm s−1, but the virtual corridors always moved at a constant speed (60 cm s−1) as long as mice kept running faster than the threshold. Running was detected using an optical tracking sensor placed close to the ball.\\n    18→\\n    19→The virtual reality corridors were created by concatenating four random crops from one of four large texture images: circle, leaf, rock and brick (Extended Data Fig. 1a). Grating stimuli (with angles of 0° and 45°) were also used to create the virtual reality corridors for a subset of mice (‘unsupervised gratings’ and VRg mice).\\n    20→\\n    21→For behaviour-only experiments, each mouse was trained with rewards on one random pair of stimuli, such as leaf–circle or rock–brick. Mice with unsupervised pretraining (VRn mice) were pretrained on the same pair on which they were trained with rewards.\\n    22→\\n    23→For imaging experiments, mice from both the task and the unsupervised cohorts were only trained on or exposed to one pair of stimuli, such as leaf–circle or rock–brick. For the mice exposed to the grating stimuli, we presented more than one pair of naturalistic stimuli before and after exposure to the gratings stimuli and recorded the neural responses to the naturalistic stimuli pairs, so each mouse can have more than one imaging session before and after. We also presented more than one pair of naturalistic stimuli to the naive mice, so each naive mouse can have more than one imaging session for testing naive responses.\\n    24→\\n    25→The two different types of leaf1-swap stimuli (Extended Data Figs. 6f and 7a) were introduced separately for task mice but are pooled together for statistics analysis. The two leaf1-swap stimuli were introduced in the same session for unsupervised and naive mice, but were treated as two different data points and pooled together for statistical analyses.\\n    26→\\n    27→Behavioural training\\n    28→\\n    29→All animals were handled via refined handling techniques for at least 3 days before being acclimated to head fixation on the ball. Animals were acclimated gradually (0.5–1 h per day) on the ball over at least 3 days until they could be head fixed without exhibiting any signs of distress. Then, animals began a running training regiment (1 h per day), which lasted for at least 5 days to ensure they could run smoothly and continuously on the ball before being exposed to the closed-loop virtual linear corridor. For water-restricted mice, we trained them for 2 days to get used to acquiring water from the spout when no stimulus was presented, before the virtual reality + reward training session. The VRn and VRg pretraining groups of mice (Fig. 5) were trained to acquire water from the spout on the last 2 days of unsupervised pretraining with no stimuli presented, after the virtual reality session ended to avoid the associative learning between stimuli and rewards. For the group without pretraining (Fig. 5), learning to get reward from the spout was similarly carried out after the running training session on the last 2 days of running training.\\n    30→\\n    31→For the behaviour-only experiment, all animals started training in the virtual reality + reward training session on a Monday and continued training for exactly 5 days. The first day of training consisted of passive reward training, during which the reward was always delivered to the mouse in the rewarded corridor at the beginning of the reward zone. The next 4 days consisted of active reward training, during which the mice were required to lick in the reward zone to trigger the reward. This ensured a consistent training schedule during the critical learning period. The beginning of the reward zone was randomly chosen per trial from a uniform distribution between 2 m and 3 m, and continued until the end of the corridor. This meant that the earliest position in the rewarded corridor in which the mouse can receive the reward was a range of 2–3 m.\\n    32→\\n    33→For imaging mice, the sound cue was presented in all trial types, for task and unsupervised mice, and the time of the sound cue was randomly chosen per trial from a uniform distribution between positions 0.5 m and 3.5 m. For task mice, the sound cue indicated the beginning of the reward zone in the rewarded corridor. The reward was delivered if a lick was detected after the sound cue in the rewarded corridor. As mice kept licking (anticipatory licking) as soon as they entered the reward corridors and learned to lick right after the sound cue, the reward delivery locations were also approximately uniformly distributed between 0.5 m and 3.5 m (Fig. 1c). In some mice, the reward was delivered passively with a delay after the sound cue, but these mice still showed anticipatory licking before the sound cue. To rule out whether the licking was due to detecting signals related to the reward delivery, such as water coming out the spout or sound produced by solenoid valve, we considered a lick response if the mouse licked at least once inside the corridor but before the sound cue. Although the rewards were absent, the sound cue was still presented in the unsupervised training experiment for consistency.\\n    34→\\n    35→Processing of calcium imaging data\\n    36→\\n    37→Calcium imaging data were processed using Suite2p32, available on GitHub (www.github.com/MouseLand/suite2p). 375→\\n   376→def get_dist_img(xpos, ypos, sel_idx=None, sig=30, sig_bg=30, xoff=800, yoff=800):\\n   377→    from scipy import ndimage\\n   378→    \\\"\\\"\\\"create an binary image for indicate  \\\\n\\\\ndef dprime(x1, x2):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"x1,x2: neurons * frames \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    u1, u2 = np.nanmean(x1, 1), np.nanmean(x2, 1)\\\\n    sig1, sig2 = np.nanstd(x1, 375→\\n   376→def get_dist_img(xpos, ypos, sel_idx=None, sig=30, sig_bg=30, xoff=800, yoff=800):\\n   377→    from scipy import ndimage\\n   378→    \\\"\\\"\\\"create an binary image for indicate 375→\\n   376→def get_dist_img(xpos, ypos, sel_idx=None, sig=30, sig_bg=30, xoff=800, yoff=800):\\n   377→    from scipy import ndimage\\n   378→    \\\"\\\"\\\"create an binary image for indicate            output_data,  # behavioral response, shape (n_output, n_timepoints) or (n_output)             ...         ],         ...     ],      '\\\"'\\\"'subjects'\\\"'\\\"': list of str, # ids of brain regions recorded from, e.g. ALM, V1     '\\\"'\\\"'brain_region_idx'\\\"'\\\"': [ # list of sessions         neuron_region_idx, # shape: (n_neurons,)     ], # index into `brain_regions` for each neuron      '\\\"'\\\"'input_names'\\\"'\\\"': list of str, # names for each input, of length n_input     '\\\"'\\\"'output_names'\\\"'\\\"': list of str, # names of each output, of length n_output     '\\\"'\\\"'output_values'\\\"'\\\"': [ # list of length n_output         [ output_val0, ... ], # list of str of length d_output[0], name of each output value         ...     ],      '\\\"'\\\"'metadata'\\\"'\\\"': {         '\\\"'\\\"'task_description'\\\"'\\\"': str, # description of output tasks         '\\\"'\\\"'time_bin_size'\\\"'\\\"': float, # length of time bin in ms         '\\\"'\\\"'temporal_alignment_event'\\\"'\\\"': str, # description of alignment event         '\\\"'\\\"'off_start'\\\"'\\\"': float or None, # signed time from alignment event to start of trial in seconds, None if N/A         '\\\"'\\\"'off_end'\\\"'\\\"': float or None, # signed time from alignment event to end of trial in seconds, None if N/A         ...     } } ```  ### Key Format Requirements  - **neural**: Neural activity data (e.g., firing rates, spike counts) organized by session and trial   - Dimensions: (n_neurons, n_timepoints) for each trial.   - Time bins should be the same size for all trials and sessions.    - There needs to be at least two trials within each session in order to evaluate the decoder performance.  - **input**: Variables that serve as inputs **to the decoder**   - These are **decoder inputs**. They could be task inputs to the animal, but inputs to the animal can also be decoder outputs.   - Examples: time from an aligning signal, stimulus characteristics, our animal behavior such as:     - visual: contrast, position, orientation     - audio: frequency, amplitude     - behavior: running speed, pupil size   - Dimensions: (d_input, n_timepoints) for each trial.    - Should capture all relevant contextual information for the decoder   - If an input is a time such as onset of some stimulus, represent it as a binary time series.   - **output**: Variables to be decoded/predicted from neural activity   - These are what we want the decoder to **predict**. They could be the animal'\\\"'\\\"'s output behavior or properties of the stimulus.   - Output variables must be **categorical**, i.e. discrete rather than continuous. If a variable is not discrete, follow instructions from Decoder Task to discretize it.    - Examples: stimulus properties (contrast, orientation), choice (left/right), reaction time, position   - Can be time-varying or discrete values per trial. If at all possible, make it time-varying   - If an output is a time such as when a behavior occurred, represent it as a binary time series.   - **subjects**: List of names of all unique subjects (mice). - **subject_idx**: Index into subjects for each session.   - Order should match order of sessions in `neural`, etc.  - **brain_regions**: List of names of all brain regions recorded from. - **brain_region_idx**: Index into brain_regions for each neuron in each session.  - **input_names**: Names of each input variable.   - Order should match order of `input` dimensions.   - **output_names**: Names of each output variable.   - Order should match order of `output` dimensions. - **output_values**: Names of each output value for each output variable.   - Order should match categorical `output` values.  - **metadata**: Descriptive information.    - `task_description`: Concise description of the task   - `temporal_alignment_event`: Concise description of temporal alignment event   - `off_start`: Signed time from alignment event to start of trial. Negative means before event, positive after.    - `off_end`: Signed time from alignment event to end of trial   - Add other relevant fields, e.g. `session_info`  ## Decoder Reference  - Run this script with `python train_decoder.py <data_file_path>` to validate. - Optional arguments:   - `--verify-only`: Only verify data format and print summary, then exit (does not train decoder).   - `--plot-samples`: Plot sample trials from data and save to png files.   - `--cpu`: Force torch to use CPU only (use if GPU runs out of memory). - Pipe the output to the designated file so that the user can examine it.  ### Purpose  These functions will be used during the validation phase to ensure: 1.
